options.content: Where the bike went and where it charged, off the decrypted ride log. Both tables drill down: click a **Started** timestamp to open that ride or that charge session, with the time range already set, in the dashboard that covers it in detail. Saved waypoints are the stars on the map and the table at the bottom; one whose position the surrounding track contradicts is listed there but not drawn. See `docs/route-map.md` for how the track is reconstructed and what the charge-stop positions actually mean, and `docs/waypoints.md` for the waypoint gate.

panels.title: Route and charge stops
panels.description:
Every GPS fix the bike logged in the window, coloured by speed, with charge stops drawn on top — sized by energy added and coloured by how stale their position is.

**The track is points, not a line, on purpose.** A line has to decide what happens across a gap, and the honest answer is *nothing*: where the bike was on a trailer, or parked with the hub asleep, there is no route to draw. Points simply stop and resume. At 1 Hz they read as a continuous track anyway.

**A charge pin is not a measured position.** This bike logs almost no GPS while charging — the Connectivity Hub sleeps — so a stop is drawn at the last fix from before it was plugged in. Green is under half an hour stale and worth trusting; red is over six hours and means only *that the bike charged*, not that it charged there.

Zoomed out the track is thinned to keep the panel responsive; narrow the range and every fix comes back. `docs/route-map.md` has the details.

**Waypoints are the stars.** A waypoint is drawn only when a logged fix on either side of it agrees with where it claims the bike was; the ones that fail are listed in the table at the bottom with the reason, because one marker nobody can vouch for reframes this whole map.

-- Route points, one per second, spikes removed.
--
-- gps_lat and gps_lon are SEPARATE log-on-change signals. They share a millisecond
-- whenever the decoder completes a fix and both moved, but a heading that only moves
-- one of them logs only that one: over the archive 53 872 lat rows and 55 191 lon rows
-- share an exact timestamp just 45 130 times. So each is carried forward onto the
-- other's timestamps rather than inner-joined, which would drop ~16 % of the track.
--
-- The 10-minute reach below $__from is the seed that carry-forward needs (see
-- grafana/README.md "Carry-forward joins need seeding from before $__from"): a window
-- opening mid-ride otherwise starts with a lat and no lon and draws nothing.
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT r.ts AS ts,
         MAX(CASE WHEN s.key = 'gps_lat'       THEN r.value END) AS lat,
         MAX(CASE WHEN s.key = 'gps_lon'       THEN r.value END) AS lon,
         -- Gated to public/lib/bounds.js's declared range for this signal. Grafana gates
         -- nothing on its own, and one 0xFFFF-ish sample destroys the colour scale for the
         -- whole track. Out of range becomes NULL (no colour), never a clamped value.
         MAX(CASE WHEN s.key = 'gps_speed_kmh' AND r.value BETWEEN 0 AND 300
                  THEN r.value END) AS speed
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key IN ('gps_lat', 'gps_lon', 'gps_speed_kmh')
    -- Reaches PAST $__to as well as below $__from, and the second half is not symmetry for
    -- its own sake: the spike test needs a point on each side, so without a successor the
    -- last point of every window is never tested. A corrupt fix landing there survives, and
    -- since the default range ends at `now` that point is the newest fix in the archive.
    -- Measured: with $__to on one of the archive's corrupt longitudes the window returned a
    -- single point ~120 deg from the track, and the map fitted half the planet.
    AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from - 600000 AND $__to + 600000
    AND r.ts < 2000000000000
  GROUP BY r.ts
),
-- SQLite has no IGNORE NULLS, so carry-forward is "the timestamp of the last non-null",
-- joined back to the row that holds it.
held AS (
  SELECT ts,
         MAX(CASE WHEN lat   IS NOT NULL THEN ts END) OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS lat_ts,
         MAX(CASE WHEN lon   IS NOT NULL THEN ts END) OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS lon_ts,
         MAX(CASE WHEN speed IS NOT NULL THEN ts END) OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS speed_ts
  FROM raw
),
paired AS (
  SELECT h.ts AS ts, la.lat AS lat, lo.lon AS lon, sp.speed AS speed
  FROM held h
  JOIN raw la ON la.ts = h.lat_ts
  JOIN raw lo ON lo.ts = h.lon_ts
  LEFT JOIN raw sp ON sp.ts = h.speed_ts
),
-- One point per second, keeping the exact last sample of each second. Without this the
-- per-millisecond pivot emits a row at each signal's own timestamp, so a lat row and a
-- lon row 1 ms apart become two points a few metres apart -- a staircase that makes
-- every implied speed nonsense (7 m in 1 ms reads as 25 000 km/h) and tricks any
-- speed-based outlier test into rejecting 2 561 perfectly good fixes.
per_second AS (
  SELECT ts, lat, lon, speed FROM (
    SELECT ts, lat, lon, speed,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ts / 1000 ORDER BY ts DESC) AS rn
    FROM paired
  ) WHERE rn = 1
),
neighbours AS (
  SELECT ts, lat, lon, speed,
         (ts - LAG(ts) OVER (ORDER BY ts)) / 1000.0        AS dt_prev,
         lat - LAG(lat)  OVER (ORDER BY ts)                AS dlat_prev,
         lon - LAG(lon)  OVER (ORDER BY ts)                AS dlon_prev,
         LEAD(lat) OVER (ORDER BY ts) - lat                AS dlat_next,
         LEAD(lon) OVER (ORDER BY ts) - lon                AS dlon_next,
         LEAD(lat) OVER (ORDER BY ts) - LAG(lat) OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS dlat_span,
         LEAD(lon) OVER (ORDER BY ts) - LAG(lon) OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS dlon_span
  FROM per_second
),
-- Spike rejection, and deliberately NOT a coordinate range gate. The bad decode produces a
-- longitude carrying an extra leading digit, landing it roughly 100 deg from the fixes one
-- second either side of it -- and such a value is still a perfectly valid longitude, so a
-- range test is really a geography test. It would also bake this bike's riding region into
-- a committed file, which is why no coordinate appears anywhere in this query.
--
-- A spike is defined by SHAPE instead: the point sits far from both neighbours WHILE THE
-- NEIGHBOURS AGREE WITH EACH OTHER. That third clause is what makes this safe without any
-- assumption about speed or sampling rate. When the bike is simply carried somewhere between
-- two fixes -- a ferry, a van, an overnight gap -- the point after the gap is also far from
-- the point before it, so the neighbours DISAGREE and the real position is kept. Only a
-- lone excursion away from a track that continues undisturbed is thrown out.
--
-- An earlier version gated on the time step instead (skip the test when dt > 120 s, on the
-- grounds that a long gap can legitimately move a long way). That let exactly two corrupt
-- fixes through, on 2026-08-09 and 2026-09-07, both in stretches where reception was sparse
-- enough that the neighbouring steps exceeded the gate. Two points out of 67 851 were enough
-- to stretch the map's auto-fit to the whole globe, which is the failure mode worth knowing:
-- a despiker on map data is not judged by the fraction it catches but by whether any survive.
--
-- Distances stay SQUARED and in degrees: no SQRT, no POW, no trig, so nothing here depends
-- on the datasource's SQLite being built with SQLITE_ENABLE_MATH_FUNCTIONS.
--
-- The test is SCALE-FREE -- "sticks out by 5x more than the neighbours are apart" -- rather
-- than a tuned distance. A fixed threshold has to be chosen for some assumed speed and
-- sampling rate, and whatever you pick is too tight when the bike is parked and too loose
-- when it is moving. The ratio has neither problem.
--
-- The 0.000004 (220 m squared, in degrees) floor is NOT a redundant belt: without it the
-- ratio degenerates exactly where d(prev, next) approaches zero, which is every second the
-- bike sits still with the hub awake. Measured over the archive's 65 481 points: the ratio
-- alone rejects 280, the ratio with this floor rejects 17, and the 263 it saves are parked
-- GPS jitter, not data. 220 m is far above that jitter and far below any real excursion.
clean AS (
  SELECT ts, lat, lon, speed, dt_prev
  FROM neighbours
  WHERE NOT (dlat_prev IS NOT NULL AND dlat_next IS NOT NULL
             AND (dlat_prev * dlat_prev + dlon_prev * dlon_prev)
                 > 25 * (dlat_span * dlat_span + dlon_span * dlon_span)
             AND (dlat_next * dlat_next + dlon_next * dlon_next)
                 > 25 * (dlat_span * dlat_span + dlon_span * dlon_span)
             AND (dlat_prev * dlat_prev + dlon_prev * dlon_prev) > 0.000004
             AND (dlat_next * dlat_next + dlon_next * dlon_next) > 0.000004)
),
-- Thin the track to a fixed budget of points. Every point is an individually styled
-- OpenLayers feature, and the whole archive is ~68 000 of them: at that size the layer stops
-- painting altogether -- tiles load, the canvas stays black, nothing is logged. 12 000 is fine.
--
-- The stride comes from the window's own row count rather than being fixed, so this is
-- self-correcting: zoom out to 90 days and points land ~6 s apart, which is sub-pixel at that
-- scale; narrow to one ride and the stride falls back to 1 and every fix is drawn.
budgeted AS (
  SELECT ts, lat, lon, speed,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS rn,
         COUNT(*) OVER ()                AS total
  FROM clean
  WHERE ts >= $__from AND ts <= $__to
)
SELECT ts / 1000.0 AS time, lat, lon, speed
FROM budgeted
-- Ceiling division: plain total / 12000 is integer division, so a 23 616-point ride day
-- gives a stride of 1 and no thinning at all -- twice the budget, and the failure is silent.
-- (rn - 1) rather than rn so the first point of the window always survives.
WHERE (rn - 1) % MAX(1, (total + 11999) / 12000) = 0
ORDER BY ts

targets.rawQueryText:
WITH evidence AS (
  SELECT r.ts AS ts
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  -- fast_dc_target_a belongs in here and its absence is not a detail: a DC session sends no
  -- 0x305/0x306 at all, so it is the ONLY DC-side current on this bus (see docs/charge-manager.md).
  -- dc_a is NOT that signal -- it is present through AC charging too, reaching 6.7 A on a day
  -- whose DC leg pulled 73 A. Detecting on mains_a/dc_a alone found 2 stops and 500 Wh across a
  -- 498 km touring day, silently missing every fast charge that made the day possible.
  WHERE s.key IN ('mains_a', 'dc_a', 'fast_dc_target_a') AND r.value > 0.5
    -- Reaches 12 h either side of the window so a session straddling an edge is seen whole.
    -- Bounded at the window instead, the evidence is clipped rather than the session excluded:
    -- a window opening mid-charge reported that charge as STARTING at the window's own `from`
    -- with a third of its energy missing, and one opening late enough dropped it entirely
    -- (its clipped span fell under the 5-minute HAVING), which also lost the ride split.
    AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from - 43200000 AND $__to + 43200000
    AND r.ts < 2000000000000
),
flagged AS (
  SELECT ts, CASE WHEN ts - LAG(ts) OVER (ORDER BY ts) < 1800000 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS is_new
  FROM evidence
),
grouped AS (
  SELECT ts, SUM(is_new) OVER (ORDER BY ts ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS g FROM flagged
),
sess AS (
  SELECT MIN(ts) AS start_ts, MAX(ts) AS end_ts
  FROM grouped GROUP BY g
  HAVING MAX(ts) - MIN(ts) >= 300000
     -- overlaps the window, having been built from evidence reaching outside it
     AND MAX(ts) >= $__from AND MIN(ts) <= $__to
),
detail AS (
  SELECT start_ts, end_ts,
         -- The AC/DC verdict rests on this and not on dc_a, for the reason above.
         (SELECT MAX(r.value) FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'fast_dc_target_a'
            AND r.ts BETWEEN sess.start_ts AND sess.end_ts) AS max_fast_dc_a,
         (SELECT MAX(r.value) FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'mains_a' AND r.ts BETWEEN sess.start_ts AND sess.end_ts) AS max_mains_a,
         -- Last known fix BEFORE plug-in, with no lower time bound: this bike logs almost
         -- no GPS while charging (0 fixes inside 33 of 37 sessions measured), because the
         -- hub sleeps. The position of a charge stop is therefore always inherited, and
         -- fix_age_min is how stale it is -- from seconds to over a week. Shown, never hidden:
         -- a three-day-old position drawn as a confident pin is the same class of lie as
         -- clamping a dead sensor into a plausible reading.
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'gps_lat' AND r.ts <= sess.start_ts AND r.ts < 2000000000000
          ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS lat,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'gps_lon' AND r.ts <= sess.start_ts AND r.ts < 2000000000000
          ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS lon,
         (SELECT r.ts FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'gps_lat' AND r.ts <= sess.start_ts AND r.ts < 2000000000000
          ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS fix_ts,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'residual_energy_wh' AND r.ts <= sess.end_ts
          ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
       - (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'residual_energy_wh' AND r.ts <= sess.start_ts
          ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS wh_added,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'soc' AND r.ts <= sess.end_ts ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS soc_end,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'soc' AND r.ts <= sess.start_ts ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS soc_start
  FROM sess
)
-- Deliberately NOT called lat/lon. Both layers bind by refId, so the naming is belt and
-- braces rather than load-bearing -- but it costs nothing and it means a layer that ever
-- loses its refId binding still cannot mistake charge stops for track.
SELECT lat AS stop_lat, lon AS stop_lon,
       ROUND(COALESCE(wh_added, 0) / 1000.0, 2)             AS "kWh added",
       ROUND((end_ts - start_ts) / 60000.0, 0)              AS "Minutes",
              -- Three-valued on purpose. fast_dc_target_a does not exist before 2026-08-26, so
       -- `> 2 ELSE 'AC'` turned its ABSENCE into a confident AC claim on every earlier
       -- session. Mains current is the positive AC evidence (it reads 0 through a DC
       -- session, which sends no 0x305/0x306 at all); with neither signal the honest
       -- answer is that this session predates the discriminator.
       CASE WHEN COALESCE(max_fast_dc_a, 0) > 2 THEN 'DC'
            WHEN COALESCE(max_mains_a, 0) > 0.5 THEN 'AC'
            ELSE '?' END                                  AS "Type",
       ROUND((start_ts - fix_ts) / 60000.0, 1)              AS "Fix age (min)",
       start_ts AS start_ms, end_ts AS end_ms
FROM detail
WHERE lat IS NOT NULL AND lon IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY start_ts

          WHERE s.key = 'residual_energy_wh' AND r.ts <= sess.end_ts

          WHERE s.key = 'residual_energy_wh' AND r.ts <= sess.start_ts
          ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS wh_added,

          WHERE s.key = 'soc' AND r.ts <= sess.end_ts ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS soc_end,

          WHERE s.key = 'soc' AND r.ts <= sess.start_ts ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS soc_start
  FROM sess

       ROUND((end_ts - start_ts) / 60000.0, 0)              AS "Minutes",

       -- session. Mains current is the positive AC evidence (it reads 0 through a DC
       -- session, which sends no 0x305/0x306 at all); with neither signal the honest
       -- answer is that this session predates the discriminator.
       CASE WHEN COALESCE(max_fast_dc_a, 0) > 2 THEN 'DC'
            WHEN COALESCE(max_mains_a, 0) > 0.5 THEN 'AC'
            ELSE '?' END                                  AS "Type",
       ROUND((start_ts - fix_ts) / 60000.0, 1)              AS "Fix age (min)",

-- Waypoints — "I am here, now", stamped into the ride log from the handlebar, the phone's
-- own button or a Siri Shortcut (src/http/waypoint.ts). Three ordinary signals, written
-- only when asked for, so they travel the same path as everything else.
--
-- ── Why this does not pivot the three signals on a shared ts ─────────────────────────
--
-- They DO share one: record() stamps all three with a single `now`, and all six waypoints
-- in the archive have identical timestamps across the three rows. But a pivot would still
-- be wrong, because record() suppresses a value equal to the last one it logged and
-- waypoint_lat/lon carry no deadband: two saves from the same live fix — two presses
-- inside one GPS gap, which is guaranteed while the fix is under FIX_MAX_AGE_MS and no new
-- sample has arrived — write only `waypoint_seq`. The pivot then yields a NULL position,
-- and SQL's three-valued logic drops that waypoint off the map AND accuses it of being
-- corrupt in the table.
--
-- So the query is driven by `waypoint_seq`, which can never be suppressed (it increments
-- inside a boot, and `lastLogged` starts empty after a restart), and each coordinate is
-- the last value logged at or before that timestamp. For a suppressed row that is the
-- previous save's coordinate — which is the same position, since suppression means the two
-- were exactly equal. Exact recovery, not an approximation.
--
-- ── The plausibility gate ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
--
-- On 2026-08-09 the bike saved a waypoint 7 000 km away. The decoder had produced a
-- longitude carrying an extra leading digit, the endpoint copied the live fix faithfully,
-- and the corrected value arrived 541 ms later. `gps_fix` was 1 and `gps_satellites` 11:
-- nothing about the fix said it was wrong.
--
-- A coordinate RANGE test cannot see that — the bad value is a perfectly legal longitude —
-- and it would also bake this bike's riding region into a committed file. So the gate is
-- CORROBORATION, in the same spirit as the track's shape test above: a waypoint is a COPY
-- of a fix, so the nearest logged fix on each side must agree with it.
--
-- ⚠️ The skew is the whole gate. A waypoint copies liveState, and gps_lat/gps_lon carry a
-- 3 m deadband, so the fix logged immediately before a waypoint IS the fix it copied — on
-- 2026-08-09 the previous gps_lon row is byte-identical to the waypoint, 148 ms earlier.
-- Comparing against it proves nothing at all. A witness at least SKEW away cannot be the
-- copy: the corruption lasted one row, and a value can only be copied while it is still
-- live.
--
-- What the skew buys, precisely: over the WHOLE archive the Aug 9 row is caught either
-- way, because the corrected fix 393 ms later objects on its own. It is at the END OF
-- DATA that the skew is the only thing left — a bike switched off straight after a
-- corrupt fix has no later fix, and then the before-side witness is the whole gate.
-- Truncated at the waypoint's own millisecond: with the skew, "contradicted" from a
-- witness 1 690 s old; without it, "on track" from a witness 0 s old, which is the
-- corrupt fix vouching for itself.
--
-- The two constants, and what bounds them:
--
--   SKEW 5 s     — above the lifetime of a corrupt fix (one row, 541 ms), and far below
--                  any distance that matters: 5 s at 200 km/h is 278 m against a 0.5°
--                  threshold of 39–55 km.
--   WINDOW 30 min — bounded BELOW by the archive: catching the Aug 9 row from the before
--                  side needs a witness 1 690 s old, which is what makes the gate work at
--                  the end of data (a bike switched off straight after a corrupt fix has
--                  no later fix to be caught by). Bounded above by the only way a witness
--                  gets that stale: at a 3 m deadband and ~1 Hz, no logged fix for 30
--                  minutes means the bike did not move — or the hub slept, which is the
--                  one case that can hide real movement, and it lands in the table as
--                  `contradicted` rather than silently on the map.
--
-- What this gate CANNOT see: docs/waypoints.md §"What each gate can see". Briefly — 0.5°
-- is 39–55 km, so the 0.3 km / 1.4 km / 4.8 km excursions this archive also contains are
-- invisible to it, and a waypoint with no witness on either side is not gated at all,
-- which is why that is a verdict of its own rather than silence.
WITH wp AS (
  SELECT r.ts AS ts, r.value AS seq
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key = 'waypoint_seq'
    AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
    AND r.ts < 2000000000000
),
placed AS (
  SELECT ts, seq,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
           WHERE s.key = 'waypoint_lat' AND r.ts <= wp.ts AND r.ts < 2000000000000
           ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS lat,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
           WHERE s.key = 'waypoint_lon' AND r.ts <= wp.ts AND r.ts < 2000000000000
           ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS lon
  FROM wp
),
-- The nearest fix on each side that is at least 5 s and at most 30 min away, per axis:
-- gps_lat and gps_lon are independently deadbanded, so on 2026-08-09 the latitude's
-- nearest witness was 19 minutes old while the longitude's was 148 ms.
witnessed AS (
  SELECT ts, seq, lat, lon,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
           WHERE s.key = 'gps_lat' AND r.ts BETWEEN placed.ts - 1800000 AND placed.ts - 5000
             AND r.ts < 2000000000000 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS lat_before,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
           WHERE s.key = 'gps_lat' AND r.ts BETWEEN placed.ts + 5000 AND placed.ts + 1800000
             AND r.ts < 2000000000000 ORDER BY r.ts LIMIT 1) AS lat_after,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
           WHERE s.key = 'gps_lon' AND r.ts BETWEEN placed.ts - 1800000 AND placed.ts - 5000
             AND r.ts < 2000000000000 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS lon_before,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
           WHERE s.key = 'gps_lon' AND r.ts BETWEEN placed.ts + 5000 AND placed.ts + 1800000
             AND r.ts < 2000000000000 ORDER BY r.ts LIMIT 1) AS lon_after
  FROM placed
),
-- COALESCE to the waypoint's own value so that "this witness does not exist" is written
-- down as "it raises no objection". It is belt and braces rather than load-bearing: a bare
-- ABS(NULL - lat) > 0.5 is NULL, `NULL OR FALSE` is NULL, no WHEN matches and the row falls
-- through to `no witness` anyway. Kept because that fall-through depends on the ORDER of
-- the arms below, and this does not — an editor moving `no witness` above `contradicted`
-- should not be able to change what a missing witness means.
--
-- ⚠️ The ±90/±180 below are a THIRD copy of LATITUDE_RANGE/LONGITUDE_RANGE in
-- src/http/waypoint.ts and public/lib/bounds.js. Only those two are asserted against each
-- other (scripts/check-waypoint-endpoint.ts); this one is on its honour.
judged AS (
  SELECT ts, seq, lat, lon,
         CASE
           WHEN lat IS NULL OR lon IS NULL THEN 'no position logged'
           WHEN lat NOT BETWEEN -90 AND 90 OR lon NOT BETWEEN -180 AND 180 THEN 'off the planet'
           WHEN ABS(COALESCE(lat_before, lat) - lat) > 0.5 OR ABS(COALESCE(lat_after, lat) - lat) > 0.5
             OR ABS(COALESCE(lon_before, lon) - lon) > 0.5 OR ABS(COALESCE(lon_after, lon) - lon) > 0.5
             THEN 'contradicted'
           -- ⚠️ PER AXIS, not "all four are missing". An axis with no witness is an axis
           -- that is not gated: its COALESCEs resolve to the waypoint's own value and
           -- object to nothing, so the other axis alone would carry the row to green.
           -- The archive holds the case — at the 2026-08-08 03:16:58 latitude spike
           -- (2.016°, ~224 km) there are 0 latitude witnesses in the band and 5 longitude
           -- ones, so a waypoint saved on it would have been drawn as `on track`.
           WHEN (lat_before IS NULL AND lat_after IS NULL)
             OR (lon_before IS NULL AND lon_after IS NULL)
             THEN 'no witness'
           ELSE 'on track'
         END AS verdict
  FROM witnessed
)
-- Only corroborated waypoints are drawn. Everything else is in the table below with its
-- verdict: this panel's view is `fit` over `allLayers`, so one uncorroborated marker
-- reframes the whole map, and a waypoint nobody can vouch for is not worth that.
SELECT ts / 1000.0 AS time, lat AS wp_lat, lon AS wp_lon, seq AS "Waypoint"
FROM judged
WHERE verdict = 'on track'
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Charge stops
panels.description: Runs where charging current actually flowed, merged across breaks under 30 minutes and counted only past 5 minutes. Built from current, not from charger_enabled — that flag is log-on-change and stays at 1 for days after the bike sleeps mid-session, which merged a 2026-08-04 charge and a 2026-08-07 charge into one 3-day 'session'.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS "Charge stops" FROM (WITH evidence AS (
  SELECT r.ts AS ts
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  -- fast_dc_target_a belongs in here and its absence is not a detail: a DC session sends no
  -- 0x305/0x306 at all, so it is the ONLY DC-side current on this bus (see docs/charge-manager.md).
  -- dc_a is NOT that signal -- it is present through AC charging too, reaching 6.7 A on a day
  -- whose DC leg pulled 73 A. Detecting on mains_a/dc_a alone found 2 stops and 500 Wh across a
  -- 498 km touring day, silently missing every fast charge that made the day possible.
  WHERE s.key IN ('mains_a', 'dc_a', 'fast_dc_target_a') AND r.value > 0.5
    -- Reaches 12 h either side of the window so a session straddling an edge is seen whole.
    -- Bounded at the window instead, the evidence is clipped rather than the session excluded:
    -- a window opening mid-charge reported that charge as STARTING at the window's own `from`
    -- with a third of its energy missing, and one opening late enough dropped it entirely
    -- (its clipped span fell under the 5-minute HAVING), which also lost the ride split.
    AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from - 43200000 AND $__to + 43200000
    AND r.ts < 2000000000000
),
flagged AS (
  SELECT ts, CASE WHEN ts - LAG(ts) OVER (ORDER BY ts) < 1800000 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS is_new
  FROM evidence
),
grouped AS (
  SELECT ts, SUM(is_new) OVER (ORDER BY ts ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS g FROM flagged
),
sess AS (
  SELECT MIN(ts) AS start_ts, MAX(ts) AS end_ts
  FROM grouped GROUP BY g
  HAVING MAX(ts) - MIN(ts) >= 300000
     -- overlaps the window, having been built from evidence reaching outside it
     AND MAX(ts) >= $__from AND MIN(ts) <= $__to
),
detail AS (
  SELECT start_ts, end_ts,
         -- The AC/DC verdict rests on this and not on dc_a, for the reason above.
         (SELECT MAX(r.value) FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'fast_dc_target_a'
            AND r.ts BETWEEN sess.start_ts AND sess.end_ts) AS max_fast_dc_a,
         (SELECT MAX(r.value) FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'mains_a' AND r.ts BETWEEN sess.start_ts AND sess.end_ts) AS max_mains_a,
         -- Last known fix BEFORE plug-in, with no lower time bound: this bike logs almost
         -- no GPS while charging (0 fixes inside 33 of 37 sessions measured), because the
         -- hub sleeps. The position of a charge stop is therefore always inherited, and
         -- fix_age_min is how stale it is -- from seconds to over a week. Shown, never hidden:
         -- a three-day-old position drawn as a confident pin is the same class of lie as
         -- clamping a dead sensor into a plausible reading.
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'gps_lat' AND r.ts <= sess.start_ts AND r.ts < 2000000000000
          ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS lat,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'gps_lon' AND r.ts <= sess.start_ts AND r.ts < 2000000000000
          ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS lon,
         (SELECT r.ts FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'gps_lat' AND r.ts <= sess.start_ts AND r.ts < 2000000000000
          ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS fix_ts,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'residual_energy_wh' AND r.ts <= sess.end_ts
          ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
       - (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'residual_energy_wh' AND r.ts <= sess.start_ts
          ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS wh_added,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'soc' AND r.ts <= sess.end_ts ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS soc_end,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'soc' AND r.ts <= sess.start_ts ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS soc_start
  FROM sess
)
SELECT
       -- Milliseconds, not seconds. The panel formats this with a `time:` display unit,
       -- which reads its input as epoch MILLIseconds -- handing it seconds renders every
       -- row as 1970-01-21 rather than erroring. (Distinct from the datasource's own
       -- `timeColumns` handling, which does want seconds; see grafana/README.md.)
       start_ts                                             AS "Started",
       ROUND((end_ts - start_ts) / 60000.0, 0)              AS "Minutes",
              -- Three-valued on purpose. fast_dc_target_a does not exist before 2026-08-26, so
       -- `> 2 ELSE 'AC'` turned its ABSENCE into a confident AC claim on every earlier
       -- session. Mains current is the positive AC evidence (it reads 0 through a DC
       -- session, which sends no 0x305/0x306 at all); with neither signal the honest
       -- answer is that this session predates the discriminator.
       CASE WHEN COALESCE(max_fast_dc_a, 0) > 2 THEN 'DC'
            WHEN COALESCE(max_mains_a, 0) > 0.5 THEN 'AC'
            ELSE '?' END                                  AS "Type",
       ROUND(COALESCE(wh_added, 0) / 1000.0, 2)             AS "kWh added",
       ROUND(soc_start, 0)                                  AS "SOC start",
       ROUND(soc_end, 0)                                    AS "SOC end",
       ROUND(max_mains_a, 1)                                AS "Peak mains A",
       ROUND(max_fast_dc_a, 1)                              AS "Peak DC A",
       CASE WHEN fix_ts IS NULL THEN NULL
            ELSE ROUND((start_ts - fix_ts) / 60000.0, 1) END AS "Fix age (min)",
       start_ts AS start_ms, end_ts AS end_ms
FROM detail

panels.title: GPS points mapped
panels.description: Points actually drawn. Mostly set by the 12 000-point render budget, not by cleanup: over the default range the chain is ~96 000 raw fixes to ~68 000 after pairing and despiking, then thinned to ~11 000 to keep the layer painting. Despiking itself rejects around 17 points in the whole archive, so this is not a data-quality number. Narrow the range and the stride falls to 1.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS "GPS points" FROM (-- Route points, one per second, spikes removed.
--
-- gps_lat and gps_lon are SEPARATE log-on-change signals. They share a millisecond
-- whenever the decoder completes a fix and both moved, but a heading that only moves
-- one of them logs only that one: over the archive 53 872 lat rows and 55 191 lon rows
-- share an exact timestamp just 45 130 times. So each is carried forward onto the
-- other's timestamps rather than inner-joined, which would drop ~16 % of the track.
--
-- The 10-minute reach below $__from is the seed that carry-forward needs (see
-- grafana/README.md "Carry-forward joins need seeding from before $__from"): a window
-- opening mid-ride otherwise starts with a lat and no lon and draws nothing.
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT r.ts AS ts,
         MAX(CASE WHEN s.key = 'gps_lat'       THEN r.value END) AS lat,
         MAX(CASE WHEN s.key = 'gps_lon'       THEN r.value END) AS lon,
         -- Gated to public/lib/bounds.js's declared range for this signal. Grafana gates
         -- nothing on its own, and one 0xFFFF-ish sample destroys the colour scale for the
         -- whole track. Out of range becomes NULL (no colour), never a clamped value.
         MAX(CASE WHEN s.key = 'gps_speed_kmh' AND r.value BETWEEN 0 AND 300
                  THEN r.value END) AS speed
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key IN ('gps_lat', 'gps_lon', 'gps_speed_kmh')
    -- Reaches PAST $__to as well as below $__from, and the second half is not symmetry for
    -- its own sake: the spike test needs a point on each side, so without a successor the
    -- last point of every window is never tested. A corrupt fix landing there survives, and
    -- since the default range ends at `now` that point is the newest fix in the archive.
    -- Measured: with $__to on one of the archive's corrupt longitudes the window returned a
    -- single point ~120 deg from the track, and the map fitted half the planet.
    AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from - 600000 AND $__to + 600000
    AND r.ts < 2000000000000
  GROUP BY r.ts
),
-- SQLite has no IGNORE NULLS, so carry-forward is "the timestamp of the last non-null",
-- joined back to the row that holds it.
held AS (
  SELECT ts,
         MAX(CASE WHEN lat   IS NOT NULL THEN ts END) OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS lat_ts,
         MAX(CASE WHEN lon   IS NOT NULL THEN ts END) OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS lon_ts,
         MAX(CASE WHEN speed IS NOT NULL THEN ts END) OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS speed_ts
  FROM raw
),
paired AS (
  SELECT h.ts AS ts, la.lat AS lat, lo.lon AS lon, sp.speed AS speed
  FROM held h
  JOIN raw la ON la.ts = h.lat_ts
  JOIN raw lo ON lo.ts = h.lon_ts
  LEFT JOIN raw sp ON sp.ts = h.speed_ts
),
-- One point per second, keeping the exact last sample of each second. Without this the
-- per-millisecond pivot emits a row at each signal's own timestamp, so a lat row and a
-- lon row 1 ms apart become two points a few metres apart -- a staircase that makes
-- every implied speed nonsense (7 m in 1 ms reads as 25 000 km/h) and tricks any
-- speed-based outlier test into rejecting 2 561 perfectly good fixes.
per_second AS (
  SELECT ts, lat, lon, speed FROM (
    SELECT ts, lat, lon, speed,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ts / 1000 ORDER BY ts DESC) AS rn
    FROM paired
  ) WHERE rn = 1
),
neighbours AS (
  SELECT ts, lat, lon, speed,
         (ts - LAG(ts) OVER (ORDER BY ts)) / 1000.0        AS dt_prev,
         lat - LAG(lat)  OVER (ORDER BY ts)                AS dlat_prev,
         lon - LAG(lon)  OVER (ORDER BY ts)                AS dlon_prev,
         LEAD(lat) OVER (ORDER BY ts) - lat                AS dlat_next,
         LEAD(lon) OVER (ORDER BY ts) - lon                AS dlon_next,
         LEAD(lat) OVER (ORDER BY ts) - LAG(lat) OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS dlat_span,
         LEAD(lon) OVER (ORDER BY ts) - LAG(lon) OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS dlon_span
  FROM per_second
),
-- Spike rejection, and deliberately NOT a coordinate range gate. The bad decode produces a
-- longitude carrying an extra leading digit, landing it roughly 100 deg from the fixes one
-- second either side of it -- and such a value is still a perfectly valid longitude, so a
-- range test is really a geography test. It would also bake this bike's riding region into
-- a committed file, which is why no coordinate appears anywhere in this query.
--
-- A spike is defined by SHAPE instead: the point sits far from both neighbours WHILE THE
-- NEIGHBOURS AGREE WITH EACH OTHER. That third clause is what makes this safe without any
-- assumption about speed or sampling rate. When the bike is simply carried somewhere between
-- two fixes -- a ferry, a van, an overnight gap -- the point after the gap is also far from
-- the point before it, so the neighbours DISAGREE and the real position is kept. Only a
-- lone excursion away from a track that continues undisturbed is thrown out.
--
-- An earlier version gated on the time step instead (skip the test when dt > 120 s, on the
-- grounds that a long gap can legitimately move a long way). That let exactly two corrupt
-- fixes through, on 2026-08-09 and 2026-09-07, both in stretches where reception was sparse
-- enough that the neighbouring steps exceeded the gate. Two points out of 67 851 were enough
-- to stretch the map's auto-fit to the whole globe, which is the failure mode worth knowing:
-- a despiker on map data is not judged by the fraction it catches but by whether any survive.
--
-- Distances stay SQUARED and in degrees: no SQRT, no POW, no trig, so nothing here depends
-- on the datasource's SQLite being built with SQLITE_ENABLE_MATH_FUNCTIONS.
--
-- The test is SCALE-FREE -- "sticks out by 5x more than the neighbours are apart" -- rather
-- than a tuned distance. A fixed threshold has to be chosen for some assumed speed and
-- sampling rate, and whatever you pick is too tight when the bike is parked and too loose
-- when it is moving. The ratio has neither problem.
--
-- The 0.000004 (220 m squared, in degrees) floor is NOT a redundant belt: without it the
-- ratio degenerates exactly where d(prev, next) approaches zero, which is every second the
-- bike sits still with the hub awake. Measured over the archive's 65 481 points: the ratio
-- alone rejects 280, the ratio with this floor rejects 17, and the 263 it saves are parked
-- GPS jitter, not data. 220 m is far above that jitter and far below any real excursion.
clean AS (
  SELECT ts, lat, lon, speed, dt_prev
  FROM neighbours
  WHERE NOT (dlat_prev IS NOT NULL AND dlat_next IS NOT NULL
             AND (dlat_prev * dlat_prev + dlon_prev * dlon_prev)
                 > 25 * (dlat_span * dlat_span + dlon_span * dlon_span)
             AND (dlat_next * dlat_next + dlon_next * dlon_next)
                 > 25 * (dlat_span * dlat_span + dlon_span * dlon_span)
             AND (dlat_prev * dlat_prev + dlon_prev * dlon_prev) > 0.000004
             AND (dlat_next * dlat_next + dlon_next * dlon_next) > 0.000004)
),
-- Thin the track to a fixed budget of points. Every point is an individually styled
-- OpenLayers feature, and the whole archive is ~68 000 of them: at that size the layer stops
-- painting altogether -- tiles load, the canvas stays black, nothing is logged. 12 000 is fine.
--
-- The stride comes from the window's own row count rather than being fixed, so this is
-- self-correcting: zoom out to 90 days and points land ~6 s apart, which is sub-pixel at that
-- scale; narrow to one ride and the stride falls back to 1 and every fix is drawn.
budgeted AS (
  SELECT ts, lat, lon, speed,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS rn,
         COUNT(*) OVER ()                AS total
  FROM clean
  WHERE ts >= $__from AND ts <= $__to
)

SELECT COUNT(*) AS "GPS points" FROM (-- Route points, one per second, spikes removed.
--
-- gps_lat and gps_lon are SEPARATE log-on-change signals. They share a millisecond
-- whenever the decoder completes a fix and both moved, but a heading that only moves
-- one of them logs only that one: over the archive 53 872 lat rows and 55 191 lon rows
-- share an exact timestamp just 45 130 times. So each is carried forward onto the
-- other's timestamps rather than inner-joined, which would drop ~16 % of the track.
--
-- The 10-minute reach below $__from is the seed that carry-forward needs (see
-- grafana/README.md "Carry-forward joins need seeding from before $__from"): a window
-- opening mid-ride otherwise starts with a lat and no lon and draws nothing.
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT r.ts AS ts,
         MAX(CASE WHEN s.key = 'gps_lat'       THEN r.value END) AS lat,
         MAX(CASE WHEN s.key = 'gps_lon'       THEN r.value END) AS lon,
         -- Gated to public/lib/bounds.js's declared range for this signal. Grafana gates
         -- nothing on its own, and one 0xFFFF-ish sample destroys the colour scale for the
         -- whole track. Out of range becomes NULL (no colour), never a clamped value.
         MAX(CASE WHEN s.key = 'gps_speed_kmh' AND r.value BETWEEN 0 AND 300
                  THEN r.value END) AS speed
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key IN ('gps_lat', 'gps_lon', 'gps_speed_kmh')
    -- Reaches PAST $__to as well as below $__from, and the second half is not symmetry for
    -- its own sake: the spike test needs a point on each side, so without a successor the
    -- last point of every window is never tested. A corrupt fix landing there survives, and
    -- since the default range ends at `now` that point is the newest fix in the archive.
    -- Measured: with $__to on one of the archive's corrupt longitudes the window returned a
    -- single point ~120 deg from the track, and the map fitted half the planet.
    AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from - 600000 AND $__to + 600000
    AND r.ts < 2000000000000
  GROUP BY r.ts
),
-- SQLite has no IGNORE NULLS, so carry-forward is "the timestamp of the last non-null",
-- joined back to the row that holds it.
held AS (
  SELECT ts,
         MAX(CASE WHEN lat   IS NOT NULL THEN ts END) OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS lat_ts,
         MAX(CASE WHEN lon   IS NOT NULL THEN ts END) OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS lon_ts,
         MAX(CASE WHEN speed IS NOT NULL THEN ts END) OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS speed_ts
  FROM raw
),
paired AS (
  SELECT h.ts AS ts, la.lat AS lat, lo.lon AS lon, sp.speed AS speed
  FROM held h
  JOIN raw la ON la.ts = h.lat_ts
  JOIN raw lo ON lo.ts = h.lon_ts
  LEFT JOIN raw sp ON sp.ts = h.speed_ts
),
-- One point per second, keeping the exact last sample of each second. Without this the
-- per-millisecond pivot emits a row at each signal's own timestamp, so a lat row and a
-- lon row 1 ms apart become two points a few metres apart -- a staircase that makes
-- every implied speed nonsense (7 m in 1 ms reads as 25 000 km/h) and tricks any
-- speed-based outlier test into rejecting 2 561 perfectly good fixes.
per_second AS (
  SELECT ts, lat, lon, speed FROM (
    SELECT ts, lat, lon, speed,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ts / 1000 ORDER BY ts DESC) AS rn
    FROM paired
  ) WHERE rn = 1
),
neighbours AS (
  SELECT ts, lat, lon, speed,
         (ts - LAG(ts) OVER (ORDER BY ts)) / 1000.0        AS dt_prev,
         lat - LAG(lat)  OVER (ORDER BY ts)                AS dlat_prev,
         lon - LAG(lon)  OVER (ORDER BY ts)                AS dlon_prev,
         LEAD(lat) OVER (ORDER BY ts) - lat                AS dlat_next,
         LEAD(lon) OVER (ORDER BY ts) - lon                AS dlon_next,
         LEAD(lat) OVER (ORDER BY ts) - LAG(lat) OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS dlat_span,
         LEAD(lon) OVER (ORDER BY ts) - LAG(lon) OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS dlon_span
  FROM per_second
),
-- Spike rejection, and deliberately NOT a coordinate range gate. The bad decode produces a
-- longitude carrying an extra leading digit, landing it roughly 100 deg from the fixes one
-- second either side of it -- and such a value is still a perfectly valid longitude, so a
-- range test is really a geography test. It would also bake this bike's riding region into
-- a committed file, which is why no coordinate appears anywhere in this query.
--
-- A spike is defined by SHAPE instead: the point sits far from both neighbours WHILE THE
-- NEIGHBOURS AGREE WITH EACH OTHER. That third clause is what makes this safe without any
-- assumption about speed or sampling rate. When the bike is simply carried somewhere between
-- two fixes -- a ferry, a van, an overnight gap -- the point after the gap is also far from
-- the point before it, so the neighbours DISAGREE and the real position is kept. Only a
-- lone excursion away from a track that continues undisturbed is thrown out.
--
-- An earlier version gated on the time step instead (skip the test when dt > 120 s, on the
-- grounds that a long gap can legitimately move a long way). That let exactly two corrupt
-- fixes through, on 2026-08-09 and 2026-09-07, both in stretches where reception was sparse
-- enough that the neighbouring steps exceeded the gate. Two points out of 67 851 were enough
-- to stretch the map's auto-fit to the whole globe, which is the failure mode worth knowing:
-- a despiker on map data is not judged by the fraction it catches but by whether any survive.
--
-- Distances stay SQUARED and in degrees: no SQRT, no POW, no trig, so nothing here depends
-- on the datasource's SQLite being built with SQLITE_ENABLE_MATH_FUNCTIONS.
--
-- The test is SCALE-FREE -- "sticks out by 5x more than the neighbours are apart" -- rather
-- than a tuned distance. A fixed threshold has to be chosen for some assumed speed and
-- sampling rate, and whatever you pick is too tight when the bike is parked and too loose
-- when it is moving. The ratio has neither problem.
--
-- The 0.000004 (220 m squared, in degrees) floor is NOT a redundant belt: without it the
-- ratio degenerates exactly where d(prev, next) approaches zero, which is every second the
-- bike sits still with the hub awake. Measured over the archive's 65 481 points: the ratio
-- alone rejects 280, the ratio with this floor rejects 17, and the 263 it saves are parked
-- GPS jitter, not data. 220 m is far above that jitter and far below any real excursion.
clean AS (
  SELECT ts, lat, lon, speed, dt_prev
  FROM neighbours
  WHERE NOT (dlat_prev IS NOT NULL AND dlat_next IS NOT NULL
             AND (dlat_prev * dlat_prev + dlon_prev * dlon_prev)
                 > 25 * (dlat_span * dlat_span + dlon_span * dlon_span)
             AND (dlat_next * dlat_next + dlon_next * dlon_next)
                 > 25 * (dlat_span * dlat_span + dlon_span * dlon_span)
             AND (dlat_prev * dlat_prev + dlon_prev * dlon_prev) > 0.000004
             AND (dlat_next * dlat_next + dlon_next * dlon_next) > 0.000004)
),
-- Thin the track to a fixed budget of points. Every point is an individually styled
-- OpenLayers feature, and the whole archive is ~68 000 of them: at that size the layer stops
-- painting altogether -- tiles load, the canvas stays black, nothing is logged. 12 000 is fine.
--
-- The stride comes from the window's own row count rather than being fixed, so this is
-- self-correcting: zoom out to 90 days and points land ~6 s apart, which is sub-pixel at that
-- scale; narrow to one ride and the stride falls back to 1 and every fix is drawn.
budgeted AS (
  SELECT ts, lat, lon, speed,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS rn,
         COUNT(*) OVER ()                AS total
  FROM clean
  WHERE ts >= $__from AND ts <= $__to
)

FROM budgeted
-- Ceiling division: plain total / 12000 is integer division, so a 23 616-point ride day
-- gives a stride of 1 and no thinning at all -- twice the budget, and the failure is silent.
-- (rn - 1) rather than rn so the first point of the window always survives.
WHERE (rn - 1) % MAX(1, (total + 11999) / 12000) = 0
ORDER BY ts
)

panels.description: One row per run of real charging current. **Fix age** is how old the position on the map was when the session started — green under 30 min, red over 6 h — because the hub sleeps while charging and almost never logs a fix inside a session. Click **Started** to open the Charging dashboard over exactly this session.

WITH evidence AS (
  SELECT r.ts AS ts
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id

  -- 0x305/0x306 at all, so it is the ONLY DC-side current on this bus (see docs/charge-manager.md).
  -- dc_a is NOT that signal -- it is present through AC charging too, reaching 6.7 A on a day
  -- whose DC leg pulled 73 A. Detecting on mains_a/dc_a alone found 2 stops and 500 Wh across a
  -- 498 km touring day, silently missing every fast charge that made the day possible.
  WHERE s.key IN ('mains_a', 'dc_a', 'fast_dc_target_a') AND r.value > 0.5
    -- Reaches 12 h either side of the window so a session straddling an edge is seen whole.
    -- Bounded at the window instead, the evidence is clipped rather than the session excluded:
    -- a window opening mid-charge reported that charge as STARTING at the window's own `from`
    -- with a third of its energy missing, and one opening late enough dropped it entirely
    -- (its clipped span fell under the 5-minute HAVING), which also lost the ride split.
    AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from - 43200000 AND $__to + 43200000
    AND r.ts < 2000000000000
),
flagged AS (
  SELECT ts, CASE WHEN ts - LAG(ts) OVER (ORDER BY ts) < 1800000 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS is_new
  FROM evidence
),
grouped AS (
  SELECT ts, SUM(is_new) OVER (ORDER BY ts ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS g FROM flagged
),
sess AS (
  SELECT MIN(ts) AS start_ts, MAX(ts) AS end_ts
  FROM grouped GROUP BY g
  HAVING MAX(ts) - MIN(ts) >= 300000
     -- overlaps the window, having been built from evidence reaching outside it
     AND MAX(ts) >= $__from AND MIN(ts) <= $__to
),
detail AS (
  SELECT start_ts, end_ts,
         -- The AC/DC verdict rests on this and not on dc_a, for the reason above.
         (SELECT MAX(r.value) FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'fast_dc_target_a'
            AND r.ts BETWEEN sess.start_ts AND sess.end_ts) AS max_fast_dc_a,
         (SELECT MAX(r.value) FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'mains_a' AND r.ts BETWEEN sess.start_ts AND sess.end_ts) AS max_mains_a,
         -- Last known fix BEFORE plug-in, with no lower time bound: this bike logs almost
         -- no GPS while charging (0 fixes inside 33 of 37 sessions measured), because the
         -- hub sleeps. The position of a charge stop is therefore always inherited, and
         -- fix_age_min is how stale it is -- from seconds to over a week. Shown, never hidden:
         -- a three-day-old position drawn as a confident pin is the same class of lie as
         -- clamping a dead sensor into a plausible reading.
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'gps_lat' AND r.ts <= sess.start_ts AND r.ts < 2000000000000
          ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS lat,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'gps_lon' AND r.ts <= sess.start_ts AND r.ts < 2000000000000
          ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS lon,
         (SELECT r.ts FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'gps_lat' AND r.ts <= sess.start_ts AND r.ts < 2000000000000
          ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS fix_ts,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'residual_energy_wh' AND r.ts <= sess.end_ts
          ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
       - (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'residual_energy_wh' AND r.ts <= sess.start_ts
          ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS wh_added,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'soc' AND r.ts <= sess.end_ts ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS soc_end,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
          WHERE s.key = 'soc' AND r.ts <= sess.start_ts ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS soc_start
  FROM sess
)
SELECT
       -- Milliseconds, not seconds. The panel formats this with a `time:` display unit,
       -- which reads its input as epoch MILLIseconds -- handing it seconds renders every
       -- row as 1970-01-21 rather than erroring. (Distinct from the datasource's own
       -- `timeColumns` handling, which does want seconds; see grafana/README.md.)
       start_ts                                             AS "Started",
       ROUND((end_ts - start_ts) / 60000.0, 0)              AS "Minutes",
              -- Three-valued on purpose. fast_dc_target_a does not exist before 2026-08-26, so
       -- `> 2 ELSE 'AC'` turned its ABSENCE into a confident AC claim on every earlier
       -- session. Mains current is the positive AC evidence (it reads 0 through a DC
       -- session, which sends no 0x305/0x306 at all); with neither signal the honest
       -- answer is that this session predates the discriminator.
       CASE WHEN COALESCE(max_fast_dc_a, 0) > 2 THEN 'DC'
            WHEN COALESCE(max_mains_a, 0) > 0.5 THEN 'AC'
            ELSE '?' END                                  AS "Type",
       ROUND(COALESCE(wh_added, 0) / 1000.0, 2)             AS "kWh added",
       ROUND(soc_start, 0)                                  AS "SOC start",
       ROUND(soc_end, 0)                                    AS "SOC end",
       ROUND(max_mains_a, 1)                                AS "Peak mains A",
       ROUND(max_fast_dc_a, 1)                              AS "Peak DC A",
       CASE WHEN fix_ts IS NULL THEN NULL
            ELSE ROUND((start_ts - fix_ts) / 60000.0, 1) END AS "Fix age (min)",
       start_ts AS start_ms, end_ts AS end_ms
FROM detail
ORDER BY start_ts DESC

panels.title: Rides
panels.description: Runs of GPS fixes separated by more than 30 minutes — **and split wherever the bike charged**, so a charge stop ends a ride rather than being counted as riding time.   FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id

    -- a window opening mid-charge reported that charge as STARTING at the window's own `from`
    -- with a third of its energy missing, and one opening late enough dropped it entirely
    -- (its clipped span fell under the 5-minute HAVING), which also lost the ride split.
    AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from - 43200000 AND $__to + 43200000
    AND r.ts < 2000000000000
),
flagged AS (
  SELECT ts, CASE WHEN ts - LAG(ts) OVER (ORDER BY ts) < 1800000 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS is_new
  FROM evidence
),
grouped AS (
  SELECT ts, SUM(is_new) OVER (ORDER BY ts ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS g FROM flagged
),
sess AS (
  SELECT MIN(ts) AS start_ts, MAX(ts) AS end_ts
  FROM grouped GROUP BY g
  HAVING MAX(ts) - MIN(ts) >= 300000
     -- overlaps the window, having been built from evidence reaching outside it
     AND MAX(ts) >= $__from AND MIN(ts) <= $__to
),
pts AS (
  SELECT r.ts AS ts
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key = 'gps_lat' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND r.ts < 2000000000000
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sess
                    WHERE r.ts BETWEEN sess.start_ts AND sess.end_ts)
),
-- Merge the fixes with the session starts into one ordered stream, so each fix can see how
-- recently a charge began without a correlated subquery per row.
stream AS (
  SELECT ts, 0 AS is_charge FROM pts
  UNION ALL
  SELECT start_ts AS ts, 1 AS is_charge FROM sess
),
tagged AS (
  SELECT ts, is_charge,
         MAX(CASE WHEN is_charge = 1 THEN ts END) OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS last_charge_ts
  FROM stream
),
fixes AS (SELECT ts, last_charge_ts FROM tagged WHERE is_charge = 0),
ride_flagged AS (
  SELECT ts,
         CASE WHEN LAG(ts) OVER (ORDER BY ts) IS NULL THEN 1
              WHEN ts - LAG(ts) OVER (ORDER BY ts) >= 1800000 THEN 1
              WHEN last_charge_ts > LAG(ts) OVER (ORDER BY ts) THEN 1
              ELSE 0 END AS is_new
  FROM fixes
),
ride_grouped AS (SELECT ts, SUM(is_new) OVER (ORDER BY ts ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS g FROM ride_flagged),
ride AS (
  SELECT MIN(ts) AS start_ts, MAX(ts) AS end_ts, COUNT(*) AS fixes
  FROM ride_grouped GROUP BY g HAVING MAX(ts) - MIN(ts) >= 300000
)
SELECT
       -- Milliseconds, not seconds. The panel formats this with a `time:` display unit,
       -- which reads its input as epoch MILLIseconds -- handing it seconds renders every
       -- row as 1970-01-21 rather than erroring. (Distinct from the datasource's own
       -- `timeColumns` handling, which does want seconds; see grafana/README.md.)
       start_ts                                 AS "Started",
       ROUND((end_ts - start_ts) / 60000.0, 0)  AS "Minutes",
       -- The bike's own odometer, not an integral of the fixes: exact, and it needs no
       -- SQRT, which keeps this query independent of how the datasource's SQLite was built.
       ROUND((SELECT MAX(r.value) - MIN(r.value) FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
              WHERE s.key = 'odometer_can_km' AND r.ts BETWEEN ride.start_ts AND ride.end_ts), 1) AS "km",
       ROUND((SELECT MAX(r.value) FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
              WHERE s.key = 'gps_speed_kmh' AND r.value BETWEEN 0 AND 300
                AND r.ts BETWEEN ride.start_ts AND ride.end_ts), 0) AS "Top km/h",
       fixes                                    AS "GPS fixes",
       start_ts AS start_ms, end_ts AS end_ms
FROM ride ORDER BY start_ts DESC

panels.title: Waypoints
panels.description: Every waypoint saved in the window — from the handlebar, the phone button or Siri. **Position** is whether the surrounding track backs it up: `on track` is drawn on the map above, anything else is listed here only. `contradicted` means a logged fix between 5 s and 30 min away puts the bike more than 0.5° from where the waypoint claims it was, which is what a corrupt GPS decode looks like. **#** restarts at 1 with the service, so it repeats. See `docs/waypoints.md`.

targets.queryText:
-- Waypoints, with the same gate the map layer applies — see this dashboard's "Route and
-- charge stops" panel for the derivation of the skew, the window and the threshold, and
-- docs/waypoints.md for what each of them can and cannot see. The query is repeated rather
-- than shared because Grafana has no way to lend one panel's CTEs to another; if you change
-- the gate here, change it there, or the map will draw a star this table calls contradicted.
WITH wp AS (
  SELECT r.ts AS ts, r.value AS seq
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key = 'waypoint_seq'
    AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
    AND r.ts < 2000000000000
),
placed AS (
  SELECT ts, seq,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
           WHERE s.key = 'waypoint_lat' AND r.ts <= wp.ts AND r.ts < 2000000000000
           ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS lat,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
           WHERE s.key = 'waypoint_lon' AND r.ts <= wp.ts AND r.ts < 2000000000000
           ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS lon
  FROM wp
),
-- The nearest fix on each side that is at least 5 s and at most 30 min away, per axis:
-- gps_lat and gps_lon are independently deadbanded, so on 2026-08-09 the latitude's
-- nearest witness was 19 minutes old while the longitude's was 148 ms.
witnessed AS (
  SELECT ts, seq, lat, lon,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
           WHERE s.key = 'gps_lat' AND r.ts BETWEEN placed.ts - 1800000 AND placed.ts - 5000
             AND r.ts < 2000000000000 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS lat_before,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
           WHERE s.key = 'gps_lat' AND r.ts BETWEEN placed.ts + 5000 AND placed.ts + 1800000
             AND r.ts < 2000000000000 ORDER BY r.ts LIMIT 1) AS lat_after,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
           WHERE s.key = 'gps_lon' AND r.ts BETWEEN placed.ts - 1800000 AND placed.ts - 5000
             AND r.ts < 2000000000000 ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1) AS lon_before,
         (SELECT r.value FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
           WHERE s.key = 'gps_lon' AND r.ts BETWEEN placed.ts + 5000 AND placed.ts + 1800000
             AND r.ts < 2000000000000 ORDER BY r.ts LIMIT 1) AS lon_after
  FROM placed
),
-- COALESCE to the waypoint's own value so that "this witness does not exist" is written
-- down as "it raises no objection". It is belt and braces rather than load-bearing: a bare
-- ABS(NULL - lat) > 0.5 is NULL, `NULL OR FALSE` is NULL, no WHEN matches and the row falls
-- through to `no witness` anyway. Kept because that fall-through depends on the ORDER of
-- the arms below, and this does not — an editor moving `no witness` above `contradicted`
-- should not be able to change what a missing witness means.
--
-- ⚠️ The ±90/±180 below are a THIRD copy of LATITUDE_RANGE/LONGITUDE_RANGE in
-- src/http/waypoint.ts and public/lib/bounds.js. Only those two are asserted against each
-- other (scripts/check-waypoint-endpoint.ts); this one is on its honour.
judged AS (
  SELECT ts, seq, lat, lon,
         CASE
           WHEN lat IS NULL OR lon IS NULL THEN 'no position logged'
           WHEN lat NOT BETWEEN -90 AND 90 OR lon NOT BETWEEN -180 AND 180 THEN 'off the planet'
           WHEN ABS(COALESCE(lat_before, lat) - lat) > 0.5 OR ABS(COALESCE(lat_after, lat) - lat) > 0.5
             OR ABS(COALESCE(lon_before, lon) - lon) > 0.5 OR ABS(COALESCE(lon_after, lon) - lon) > 0.5
             THEN 'contradicted'
           -- ⚠️ PER AXIS, not "all four are missing". An axis with no witness is an axis
           -- that is not gated: its COALESCEs resolve to the waypoint's own value and
           -- object to nothing, so the other axis alone would carry the row to green.
           -- The archive holds the case — at the 2026-08-08 03:16:58 latitude spike
           -- (2.016°, ~224 km) there are 0 latitude witnesses in the band and 5 longitude
           -- ones, so a waypoint saved on it would have been drawn as `on track`.
           WHEN (lat_before IS NULL AND lat_after IS NULL)
             OR (lon_before IS NULL AND lon_after IS NULL)
             THEN 'no witness'
           ELSE 'on track'
         END AS verdict
  FROM witnessed
)
-- Every waypoint in the window, including the ones the map refuses to draw. A rejected
-- reading is shown as a fault and never silently dropped — public/lib/bounds.js's rule,
-- and the reason this table is not merely a convenience.
--
-- `#` repeats: waypoint_seq counts within one boot of the service and starts over at 1
-- when it restarts. Three rows in the archive carry `1`, from three different boots.
SELECT ts       AS "Saved",
       seq      AS "#",
       lat      AS "Latitude",
       lon      AS "Longitude",
       verdict  AS "Position"
FROM judged
ORDER BY ts DESC
